title: Operating Lines of Credit — Overadvance Tolerance, Fee Rate and Cure Period by Product
content:
An overadvance is an advance on one of the Operating Lines of Credit that goes beyond the line's available credit. Whether a product allows it, at what price and for how long is fixed product by product.

## Terms

- **Overadvance tolerance**: advances may exceed the available credit by up to this percentage of the commitment as a priced overadvance; 0 means no overadvance is permitted.
- **Overadvance fee rate**: the fee on the portion of an advance that exceeds the available credit, as a percentage of that portion.
- **Overadvance cure period**: the calendar days after an overadvance is booked by which principal must be back within the available credit; 0 means not applicable.

## Schedule

| Product | Overadvance tolerance (% of commitment) | Overadvance fee rate (% of the excess) | Cure period (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| StartRight Operating Line | 0 (none permitted) | 0 | 0 |
| ExpressLine Operating Credit | 0 (none permitted) | 0 | 0 |
| Seasonal Operating Loan | 0 (none permitted) | 0 | 0 |
| Revolving Operating Line | 0 (none permitted) | 0 | 0 |
| Borrowing Base Operating Line | 5 | 1.00 (1) | 30 |
| Agribusiness Revolving Line | 7.5 | 0.75 | 45 |

## Points of reading

- Only the Borrowing Base Operating Line and the Agribusiness Revolving Line permit an overadvance at all.
- The tolerance is measured against the commitment, not against the available credit. *Hypothetical illustration:* on a Borrowing Base Operating Line with a USD 2,000,000 commitment, 5% of the commitment is a tolerance of USD 100,000; on an Agribusiness Revolving Line with the same commitment, 7.5% is USD 150,000.
